hn-50589618.t: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis
hn-50589618.s: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis Joint statement by the Lean and Mathlib communities, endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative. On November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge released a pro
ex: Joint statement by the Lean and Mathlib communities, endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative. On November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as a Lean library comprising 17 million lines of code. We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him on this achievement. The codebase depends directly only on Mathlib. Over the past day, the Lean and Mathlib communities have rallied to verify the proof's correctness. We hereby certify that both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis are correct. The four criteria in https://xenaproject.wordpress.com/2026/11/12/and-the-proof-is-checked-in-lean/ are all satisfied. Thanks are owed to everyone in the community who provided resources for the verification. We look forward to all the activity in the mathematical community that will help explain the new ideas in this proof.

hn-50591853.s: A quantization compiler that delivers 12× lower KL than Q4_K_M at the same file size
ex: LookAtMyQuant is a quantization compiler. It measures how much each stored piece of a model hurts the output when compressed. It then picks a code for each piece so the whole model fits a size budget with the least damage. On Gemma 4 E2B, its GGUF has 12× lower KL than Q4KM at the same file size. The method and every result are on the site. LookAtMyQuant 2 takes Qwen3.5-4B to 1.23 GB, 2.3 bits per weight. The file solves 330 of 540 exact-answer math problems. Prism ML's Bonsai 2 Ternary 4B solves 328 at 1.20 GB, and the original solves 359. Its KL from the original on held-out text is 0.45 nats, against 0.59 for Bonsai. The recipe is post-training quantization with trellis codes, calibrated on the model's own worked math solutions with digit tokens weighted 10×, and with bits allocated per row by Fisher information. 4,000 steps of distillation follow, in which every layer is re-quantized once from the original weights.

hn-50590279.t: Zero C# – C# without a runtime or GC
hn-50590279.s: A bflat fork that compiles C# to small native programs with no .NET runtime and no garbage collector, for Linux, macOS, Windows, WebAssembly and DOS on a 386.
ex: A fork of bflat compiles C# straight to a small native program: no .NET runtime, no garbage collector, nothing to install where it runs. You keep C#'s syntax, type checking and generics. Memory comes from arenas you free all at once, and a small library gives you strings, collections, input and output on those terms. The same source runs on Linux, macOS and Windows, on WebAssembly, and on DOS on a 386. The compiler still checks everything it checks in .NET. What's missing is what a runtime would do while your program runs. The hello-world sample, unchanged, built for each target. Each build is checked by the same test suite, which requires the same output everywhere. A native program that needs only the C library. On macOS it builds and runs in a container. A native Mac program: bflat compiles it, the Mac's own clang links it. No container to run it. A console program on Windows' own C library, built from Linux or macOS. Tested under Wine.

hn-50586292.t: ClawDOS – An AI coding agent for DOS
hn-50586292.s: An AI chat and coding harness for DOS, on a real IBM PC 5160 (8088 at 4.77 MHz)
ex: An AI coding agent for DOS. It runs on an IBM PC XT: an 8088 at 4.77 MHz, 640K of RAM, a CGA card. Backstory: The IBM PC was my first computer. Rather, it was my parents’ first personal computer that I got to use at a very early age. It was already obsolete by the time I was old enough to use it, but at 5 years old it was a magical device that I could make do different things depending on what I typed. I learned how to type and use DOS so that I could launch some early “Learn the Alphabet” games that my mom had bought me. I learned some elementary-level use of BASIC, but at the time that didn’t progress much further than making some number guessing games and other small projects. From there, many years passed but I still have some of the original parts of that PC. I have a collection of vintage machines that mean something to me, with my fully maxed-out IBM PC 5160 being the centerpiece of my collection.

hn-50591260.s: Build PostgreSQL extensions from plain Go code, using TinyGo: functions marked with //gopgext:function become SQL functions.
ex: gopgext builds PostgreSQL extensions from plain Go code, using TinyGo. Mark a function with //gopgext:function and it becomes a SQL function: gopgext writes the C glue, the install script and the control file. A project is plain Go files. The standard library works: fmt, regexp, encoding/json, crypto/*, maps, generics, iterators, defer/recover. Strings, numbers, arrays, NULLs, sets, rows, timestamps, UUIDs and JSON map to SQL types. Define your own data types and composite types in Go. Run SQL through SPI, return errors with SQLSTATE codes, log, read settings and stay responsive to query cancellation. Write triggers, aggregates, GiST, GIN, SP-GiST and BRIN operator classes, index access methods, foreign data wrappers and query hooks. Ports of PostgreSQL’s contrib modules (pgcrypto, hstore, pg_stat_statements, cube, …) pass upstream’s regression tests. Several Go extensions load in one backend.

gh-1466548112.s: AI App Builder: Prompt to Full-Stack Next.js Apps with Hosting, Database, Auth, and Multitenancy
ex: AI App Builder transforms a plain-language prompt into a complete, production-ready Next.js application—with hosting, database, authentication, AI integration, bidirectional GitHub sync, multitenancy, and custom domains already wired in. It is a polished, self-hostable alternative for teams and independent builders who want to ship full-stack apps without assembling infrastructure piece by piece. Every project runs in an isolated sandbox observed through a live preview, visual editor, and full code editor, so ideas move from description to deployed product in a single, guided flow. The result is an approachable, white-label platform that fits just as naturally inside your own product as it does on its own. - OS: Windows 10 / 11 - Shell: PowerShell 5.1+ or PowerShell 7+ - Network: internet access to download the script - Privileges: standard user Prompt to Full-Stack App.

gh-1466272233.s: Open-source, local-first AI agent team for your desktop: multi-agent group chats, computer use, browser, MCP, routines and approvals. macOS, Windows, Linux + Android. Built on pi.
ex: An open-source, local-first AI agent team for your desktop. Named AI Bots work on your own computer: chat with one or put several in a group chat, and they plan, run commands, edit files, browse the web and use your computer, while every risky step waits for your approval. Runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, with an Android app. Built on the pi agent kernel. Pi Bot is a desktop app in which a team of named Bots works on your own computer. You chat with a Bot directly or put several in a group chat, give them a working folder, and they plan, run commands, edit files and hand work to each other, while every risky step waits for your approval. The "brain" runs on your machine too: chats, files, memory and keys stay local, and only the model provider you choose sees the prompts you send. - Bots and roles. Create Bots with a name, a role (developer, researcher, writer, translator, …), their own model, skills, permissions and memory. - Direct and group chats.

hn-50587875.t: My monitor was cutting my download speed by 75%
hn-50587875.s: Upload at 2.4 Gbps, download at 600 Mbps, same cable and same adapter. Here's how I tracked it down to my Studio Display XDR, a tiny buffer, and a USB burst size of four packets.
ex: Somehow I am one of those few very lucky people to have the opportunity of owning a 2.5 gig symmetrical line for my internet. But one day, when I wanted to brag to my equally nerdy friends, shock and horror: 600 Mbps down? Luckily my upload speed was still 2.4 Gbps, so I didn’t lose all my bragging rights, but that’s weird, right? If anything, you’d expect the opposite! My ISP is pretty cool. It’s run by this one guy (Hey Keith!), and I know I can always message them and they respond promptly, as they did this time. We tried to run through a few debugging steps, they checked on their end, and everything was normal. I tried my work laptop too, same speed. I didn’t have time for debugging, because I needed to travel 2000 km to the other side of the continent for a family emergency. But as soon as I got back, I got curious again. What could it be? In retrospect, I now know when it started: when I moved all my connections onto my Studio Display XDR.

hn-50582069.t: Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as 'biggest breakthrough in decades'
hn-50582069.s: Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing
ex: Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades. In one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib, during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. The trial participants had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body. Though doctors have said the pill cannot yet be considered a cure, and they do not know how long it can keep the disease at bay, they have said it is encouraging news because it appears it will offer patients more time, even if it does not cause full remission.

hn-50583028.t: Getting the mind to steer the body to steer you
hn-50583028.s: Often in life, your body is the one steering you.
ex: Often in life, your body is the one steering you. And sometimes, to get to do the thing you want, you can’t just convince yourself with reason or arguments, or will yourself, or do the exercises to get there - you need to learn the magic formula, the secret words, to trick the body into acting in a way that gets you the outcome you want. As a kid, spending time on the internet forums for bands I loved, I kept hearing about some magical book called The Easy Way to Stop Smoking by Allen Carr, that cured people of their smoking addiction. Middle-aged man after middle-aged man would praise the miracles of this book - not by the patch, not by gum, not by sheer will, only by reading this book could they quit smoking - and not only that, everyone they had given the book to had the same result. As a 12 year old, unable to find out what this book actually said, I spent hours thinking about this - trying to figure out what secret trick the book could be sharing that was so powerful.

hn-50577991.s: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that every developer blog begins by explaining the new static site generator they wrote to make it.
ex: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that every developer blog begins by explaining the new static site generator they wrote to make it. This post isn’t exactly that, but maybe only on a technicality, in that it’s not about this website… Earlier this year I decided to put a some of my paintings and sketchbook pages online. I don’t much use social media besides Hacker News, but I wanted to share my work with friends and family. So I’d been sending scans of my work in group chats. That was fine for a bit but so messy and disorganized. Sometimes someone asked, “Where did you paint this?” Sometimes a friend wanted to see what it looked like in real life. My little brother suggested a map with a marker for each piece. That was a good idea! For that I’d need a website and some code. Here, take a look at the map, its done now! You can zoom and click on markers to see the painting! When it comes to tech side projects there are two wolves inside me.

lb-hcofqi.t: Probabilistic data structures in Go, part 2
lb-hcofqi.s: Binary fuse filter, UltraLogLog, Log-linear histogram, and MinHash.
ex: Probabilistic data structures give you approximate answers to questions about the data they handle. Does the set contain a certain item? How many unique items are in the collection? What is the 99th percentile in a stream of numbers? How similar are two sets? Unlike deterministic structures, the answers might not be exact, but in return, you can save a lot of memory. Previously, we reviewed the following data structures: Bloom filter (for checking if an item is in a set), Count-min sketch (for counting items), HyperLogLog (for counting unique items), T-digest (for finding quantiles), and Top-k (for finding the most frequent items). In this post, we'll talk about other probabilistic structures and compare them to the ones we've already covered. We'll look at how they work and what kinds of guarantees they provide. All examples use unsure — a package that implements these structures in Go.

gh-1465855400.s: Leonida Is A Native PC Recompilation Of The Xbox Version Of Grand Theft Auto 6
ex: Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy. Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens on your PC, from your own copy of the game. Early. The game does not boot yet. Everything that can be done without the game's executable is in place, so work on booting can start as soon as one is available to a developer. The port isn't downloaded ready-made. It's built on your PC from your own copy. 1. Install the prerequisites below. 2. Download this project with its submodule: git clone --recursive https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out thirdparty/rpf9-explorer.

gh-1465728637.s: Static recompilation research for Xbox Series X|S (Scarlett) on x64 Windows, including shader translation, BC7 textures, script-state replay and D3D12/PE checks.
ex: Xbox2Windows investigates static recompilation of Xbox Series X|S (Scarlett) software for x64 Windows. The CPU experiments translate source-built x64 functions from PE machine code through C++ to Windows executables and DLLs. A source-built EXE now runs end to end from its translated entry through an internal call and a named DLL import. The shader experiment translates selected gfx1013 pixel shaders through HLSL to desktop DXIL. Other experiments test the Windows runtime, render recovered texture levels and read script state data. Title CPU code execution, full-game startup and frame rate remain unverified. New to the project? The pinned guide in GitHub Discussions will help you choose a first contribution. Ask build and debugging questions in Development Q&A. The public suite builds its own fixtures. A contributor can reproduce the checks below on a PC without a game installation. The standalone release packages the GPU check.
